institution: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi
citation: Institute of Clinical Microbiology and Immunology, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital. Clinical Microbiology Newsletter, Vol. 30 (1) and 31 (1): percentage sensitivity, January 2023 to December 2024. New Delhi: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital; published July 2025.
reporting: Percent susceptible by specimen (blood, urine, pus/tissue, body fluids, respiratory specimens), organism (Gram-positive and Gram-negative tables) and location (OPD, ward, ICU), with the number of isolates per row; organism counts per specimen and location in bar charts with printed data labels and an "others" list.
method: MIC testing on Vitek 2, interpreted with CLSI 2023 and 2024 guidelines; repeat isolates excluded (printed in parentheses); two years of data combined (Vol. 30 (1) and 31 (1)) to improve denominators.

verification.note: All 10 susceptibility tables (GPC and GNB, pages 2 to 6) were parsed from the PDF text layer (pdfplumber word positions; column headers rebuilt from the rotated header text; OPD, ward and ICU taken from each row's background colour and checked against the row order), then every cell and every row n was compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 4 and cropped into left and right halves: no differences. Organism charts: legend and "others" entries were parsed from the text layer, checked arithmetically per panel (legend counts plus Others equal the printed Isolates, "others" entries sum to Others, legend counts equal the bar data labels) and compared by eye with the rendered charts. Two legend entries with a garbled number were read from the image and the bar label (blood ICU "E. coli1-53", bar 153; urine OPD "E. coli1-370", bar 1370), and one "others" entry the parser missed (pus OPD "Providencia spp.1-") was added from the image.

notes: Clinical Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 30 (1) and 31 (1), two years combined (January 2023 to December 2024), 8 pages. Pages 2 to 6 give one specimen each (blood; urine; pus/tissue; body fluids; respiratory specimens): organism bar charts for OPD, ward and ICU (samples, positives, isolates, legend counts and an "others" list) and Gram-positive (GPC) and Gram-negative (GNB) percentage sensitivity tables with three rows per organism (OPD, ward, ICU, by the colour key) and the number of isolates; "-" means not done. Specimens recorded as blood, urine, pus (printed "Pus / Tissue", pus and tissue reported together), sterile (printed "Body fluids") and respiratory. Rows printed "Staphylococcus spp." (pus: "Staphylococci spp.") are separate from Staph. aureus and are recorded as coagulase-negative staphylococci, as the 2011 edition labels the same row "Staphylococci spp. (CONS)". Combined columns: "Cefoxitin/Oxacillin" is recorded under oxacillin, "Imipenem/Meropenem" (blood and body fluid GNB tables) under meropenem, and "Glycopeptides" under vancomycin (vancomycin and teicoplanin reported as one figure; the 2011 edition heads the same column "Vancomycin/Teicoplanin"); each such cell says so in its note. The "Quinolones" column (no agent named) is not recorded. Blood S. pneumoniae: penicillin and ceftriaxone hold the non-meningitis breakpoint columns; the meningitis-breakpoint values are in the cell notes. Urine and pus imipenem is printed "*Imipenem" with a footnote advising an alternative method before reporting Vitek 2 imipenem results for Proteus, Morganella and Providencia (noted on the Proteus cells). Colistin is not reported: the newsletter states that CLSI has had no susceptible category for colistin in Gram-negative bacteria since 2020. Fungal isolates are counted in the charts but their susceptibility data were deferred to the next issue. Isolate numbers: the charts and the tables disagree by one isolate for 10 organism strata (blood ICU E. coli; urine ward E. coli and E. faecalis; urine ICU E. coli and P. aeruginosa; pus OPD K. pneumoniae; pus ward and body fluid OPD coagulase-negative staphylococci; body fluid ward E. coli and K. pneumoniae); each is recorded as printed and noted on its row. The body fluid ICU "others" list sums to 49 against "Others-50". Some percentages are not what rounding gives for the row's n (urine ICU Proteus n=12 prints cefuroxime 41 where 5/12 is 41.7, which suggests truncation), and a few match no count of the row's isolates at all (body fluid OPD Enterobacter n=13, cefepime 66; respiratory ward S. pneumoniae n=21, penicillin and ceftriaxone 97): per-drug tested numbers are not printed; all are recorded as printed. Organism counts: every legend and "others" entry whose organism has a canonical key is recorded, with misspellings mapped to the intended organism ("Klebseilla", "Serratia marscecens", "Elizebethkingia meninseptica", "Sphinmonas paucimobilis", "Neisseria norrhoeae", "L.monocytogenes"); "Salmonella entertidis" is recorded as non-typhoidal Salmonella and "Serratia odorifera" as Serratia spp.; entries without a key, or that would add to the key of a tabulated organism, are listed in excluded. Page 1 and 8 (case report, publications, highlights) and page 7 (antimicrobial consumption) are not susceptibility tables.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 1,043 cells (the seeded 25% sample of 261 from sample_cells.py, spread over all 10 GPC and GNB tables on pages 2 to 6, plus every other cell), all 115 row n values and all 279 organism counts were read from the page images (tables at scale 3 cut into halves with the row labels kept; chart legends and "others" lists at scale 5, scale 8 where needed) before comparing with the extraction. An independent word-position parse of the PDF text layer agreed with that reading on all 129 printed table rows (n and every cell, dashes included).

Result: 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected. No wrong value or n; OPD, ward and ICU correct on every row (also confirmed from the yellow, blue and pink row fills); organism and specimen correct on every row; every printed value of a recorded column is in the file. The 14 table rows not recorded are exactly the 13 rows printed all "-" plus blood S. Paratyphi A ICU (n=1, Quinolones 0 only), as excluded says. No table exceeded the 2% error threshold, but every table was re-read in full anyway.

Combined columns: all 18 Cefoxitin/Oxacillin cells (under oxacillin), all 23 Imipenem/Meropenem cells (under meropenem, blood and body fluid GNB) and all 41 Glycopeptides cells (under vancomycin) carry their cell note; the 4 blood S. pneumoniae non-meningitis cells carry the meningitis values (penicillin 41 OPD and 33 ICU, ceftriaxone 83 and 83), and the *Imipenem footnote is noted on the 6 Proteus cells.

Cells the build does not keep, all printed that way (not transcription errors): Proteus urine nitrofurantoin 0 in OPD, ward and ICU and Proteus pus minocycline 8, 9 and 15 (intrinsic); body fluid OPD CoNS penicillin 8 while the same row prints Cefoxitin/Oxacillin 0 (suppressed, source inconsistency); respiratory ward S. pneumoniae penicillin 97 and ceftriaxone 97 with n = 21 (caution, conflict entries).

Count mismatches, all printed that way (organism chart one more than the table n, each noted on its row): blood ICU E. coli 153 and 152; urine ward E. coli 498 and 497, E. faecalis 38 and 37; urine ICU E. coli 220 and 219, P. aeruginosa 68 and 67; pus OPD K. pneumoniae 357 and 356; pus ward CoNS 46 and 45; body fluid OPD CoNS 13 and 12; body fluid ward K. pneumoniae 88 and 87, E. coli 100 and 99.

Also as printed, and not visible to the build because the table row is all "-" and not recorded: body fluid ICU "Staphylococcus spp." is 9 in the chart's "others" list and 8 in the GPC table. The body fluid ICU "others" list sums to 49 against "Others-50" (read at scale 8). Every other panel adds up: legend entries plus Others equal the printed Isolates, the "others" entries sum to Others, and every bar label equals its legend entry.
